# encrypt.aauth.dev

> A send service. Sends an end-to-end encrypted message for an agent: it takes the sender's address, the recipient, and the text; fetches the recipient's latest key from the messaging service, encrypts (a compact JWE, ECDH-ES A256GCM, P-256), and uploads the JWE there, acting for the person over an AAuth call chain. An AAuth resource (access_mode: person-token). Stateless; sees the plaintext, stores nothing. Open code, self-hostable.

Reach it with the AAuth MCP: `connect_resources {items: [{resource: "encrypt.aauth.dev"}]}` (the person approves one card; this service sees plaintext), then `invoke {resource: "encrypt.aauth.dev", op_id: "sendMessage", body: {from, to, text}}`. Put the fields directly in `body`.

A person's account at the messaging service names their send service as `send_message_with {resource, op_id}`. This host is the default for secret.agent.coop.

## The operation

`sendMessage {from, to, text, resource?, idempotency_key?}`

- `from`: required. One of the sender's addresses at the messaging service, e.g. `mailto:you@example.com`, in any spelling.
- `to`: the recipient's address there: `peer_address` on the connection.
- `text`: the message, up to 64 KB. Text only (no attachments yet).
- `resource`: the messaging service to deliver through, as an https origin. Optional; the default is `https://secret.agent.coop`. A person using another messaging service names it here.
- `idempotency_key`: optional; a repeat with the same key returns the first message with `replayed: true`.

Returns `{id, from, to, kid, size, resource}`, with `from` and `to` as the messaging service shows them.

What it does: a person token for `resource` over the chain; `getPublicKey {from, to}` there; encrypt `{"text": …}`; `uploadMessage {from, to, jwe}` there. If the recipient rotated their key in between (`409 key_rotated`), it fetches the key again and retries once.

Refusals from the messaging service pass through with `step: get_public_key | upload_message`: `not_connected` (404: the person must invite them first), `recipient_has_no_key` (409: they have not finished createAccount), `rate_limited` (429), `invalid_request` with `field: from` (400: not one of the sender's addresses). `text_too_long` (413) and `attachments_not_supported` (400) are this service's. A 502 with `step: person_token` means the Person Server refused a token for `resource` (`error` is its code); `resource_unreachable` means the messaging service did not answer.

The recipient reads with `listMessages` at the messaging service, then `readMessage {id}` at their read service (default https://decrypt.aauth.dev).

- Agent document (call chaining, `aauth:send@encrypt.aauth.dev`): https://encrypt.aauth.dev/.well-known/aauth-agent.json

- The matching read service: https://decrypt.aauth.dev/llms.txt
